quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and use your mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if it is safe to change lanes.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Allow you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you safe. It helps you stay out of blind spots, see better, avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space:

options.text: Should always stay the same.
Should vary according to riding conditions.
Is not necessary in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should vary according to riding conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop, the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy. Always increase your distance from other vehicles in these situations.

questions.question: Motorists entering a highway from an entrance ramp to your right may not see your motorcycle. To help the entering drivers, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Flash your lights.
Move to the left portion of your lane so they can share the lane, if necessary.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles entering the highway. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Find a lane position that allows the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride in the right side of the lane to be visible to other motorists.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Alternate between the left and center lane positions so you attract the attention of other motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a lane position that allows the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors, so this position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, you will want to adjust the:

options.text: Brakes.
Seat.
Suspension.
Brake light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the added weight.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Means that they see you.
Will never happen.
Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not trust eye contact. Drivers may look at you but still not notice you. Never assume they will yield to you just because they made eye contact.

questions.question: If you are transporting a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean as you lean.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you as you turn. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Ride in a position that will allow the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver sees you.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a position that will allow the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of the lane so you appear in the middle of the driver's rearview mirror. This is where drivers are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Only take a few minutes.
Take more than an hour.
Be complicated to perform.
Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only take a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection to:

options.text: See if parked vehicles are entering traffic.
Look for vehicles changing lanes.
Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
See if someone is planning to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to check for cars approaching from behind. Drivers may not see you until they are too close. You need time to react.

questions.question: Under Nevada law, a moped cannot have a displacement of more than:

options.text: 25 cubic centimeters.
50 cubic centimeters.
75 cubic centimeters.
100 cubic centimeters.

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 cubic centimeters.
questions.explanation: Nevada law defines a moped as a motor scooter or cycle with an engine of no more than 50 cubic centimeters.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Coming to a complete stop before you expect to.
Popping a tire.
Taking too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, focus on:

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
Your arms.
The road in front of your motorcycle.
The side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the side lane as possible. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while taking a curve is often caused by:

options.text: Taking the turn too fast.
Lanes that are too narrow.
Not knowing how to steer.
Lanes that are too wide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Taking a curve at too high a speed may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, avoid the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
Is only useful for protecting riders from dirt.
Does not offer as much protection as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: When should your rearview mirror be adjusted?

options.text: After starting the motorcycle.
Before starting the motorcycle.
During the ride.
At a traffic signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Adjust them to see the lane behind you and as much of the side lane as possible.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
In the left part of your lane.
In the right part of your lane.
Move back and forth across your lane as they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the same following distance as usual.
Brake later than you normally would.
Ride slower than usual.
Ride faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger makes your motorcycle sit lower. Ride slower than usual, especially through curves and bumps. The extra weight also means your motorcycle speeds up, slows down, and stops more slowly. Keep more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the road edge.
Use both brakes and stop as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the road edge.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle while staying straight. If you must brake, slowly apply only the brake on the tire that is still good. Move toward the road edge as you slow down, then stop.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load placed too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes the motorcycle less balanced.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, what happens to acceleration and braking?

options.text: Acceleration takes less time, but braking takes more time.
Both acceleration and braking take more time.
Acceleration takes more time, but braking takes less time.
Both acceleration and braking take less time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both acceleration and braking take more time.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo slows down acceleration and braking. Your motorcycle takes longer to speed up and stop.
